growing_specifications.description: Rapid-cycling leafy brassica staple across Philippine lowlands, highlands, and urban container gardens. Features upright rosettes with succulent porcelain-white petioles, glossy dark green foliage, shallow fibrous roots, and year-round commercial harvest versatility.

category_why.title: Why is Pechay classified under Leafy Greens (Brassicaceae)?
category_why.summary: Brassica rapa subsp. chinensis is an upright leafy rosette vegetable harvested for its succulent white petioles and dark green leaves before reproductive flowering.
points: Upright Rosette Growth: Forms a 20–30 cm tall cluster of broad, glossy dark green leaves connected to thick, crisp white petioles (stalks).
Rapid Vegetative Cycling: One of the fastest-cycling crops in the Philippines, reaching early harvest in 25–35 days and full maturity in 30–45 days.
Culinary & Economic Staple: Vital fresh ingredient in Philippine cooking (nilaga, bulalo, sinigang, stir-fries), enabling 8 to 10 sequential cropping cycles annually.

harvest_why.title: Why is Pechay harvested at 25–40 days before bolting?
harvest_why.summary: Harvesting at peak rosette expansion preserves tender, crisp, succulent petioles before high temperatures trigger yellow flower stalk development.
points: Sprout & Emergence (Days 3–7): Small true seeds sprout quickly at 0.5–1.0 cm shallow planting depth.
Seedling & Nursery Phase (Days 7–14): Seedlings develop 3–4 true leaves with heart-shaped cotyledons, ready for transplanting or thinning.
Rapid Vegetative Expansion (Days 14–25): Fast foliar expansion and petiole thickening driven by nitrogen and soil moisture.
Early Harvest & Baby Pechay (Days 25–30): Tender 150–250 g bunches ideal for quick stir-fry and light soups.
Full Market Maturity (Days 30–40): Robust 250–400 g bunches with thick, porcelain-white crisp petioles.
Bolting Deterioration Post-40–45 Days: Prolonged heat and photoperiods trigger yellow flowering (bolting), turning petioles tough, fibrous, and bitter.

watering_why.title: Why does Pechay require daily to alternate-day shallow irrigation?
watering_why.summary: A shallow fibrous root system (5–10 cm depth) demands steady topsoil moisture to sustain succulent white stems without leaf wilting or toughness.
points: Surface Root Fragility: Roots concentrate strictly within the upper 10 cm of the soil profile, rapidly depleting surface moisture on hot sunny days.
Crispness & Tenderness: Water deficits cause petioles to become stringy, tough, and fibrous with premature flowering.
Morning Irrigation Protocol: Watering at 6:00–7:30 AM avoids splashing muddy soil into inner leaf axes and ensures foliage dries before nightfall, suppressing bacterial soft rot.

soil_why.title: Why does Pechay thrive in well-drained loam (pH 6.0–6.8) on 15–20 cm raised beds?
soil_why.summary: Loose organic-rich loam supports fast root penetration while raised beds safeguard against waterlogging, damping-off, and bacterial soft rot.
points: Raised Bed Drainage: 15–20 cm raised beds with 30 cm drainage furrows prevent stagnant standing water during heavy tropical downpours.
Nitrogen & Boron Balance: Rich compost and pH 6.0–6.8 ensure balanced uptake of Nitrogen (100–150 kg/ha) for lush leaves and Boron to prevent Hollow Stem (cracked petioles).
Soil Aeration & Damping-off Control: Friable loose loam prevents compaction, reducing seedling mortality from soil-borne Pythium and Rhizoctonia.

varieties.description: The premier nationwide commercial open-pollinated variety in the Philippines. Features broad, glossy, dark green leaves and thick, pure white, crisp petioles with excellent heat and moderate rain tolerance.
High-vigor hybrid cultivar bred for rapid establishment, uniform growth, heavy bunch weight, and resilience against common leaf spots.
Compact, spoon-shaped variety with tender jade-green petioles and sweet flavor. Extremely popular for rapid-cycle urban hydroponics and gourmet stir-fries.
Thick, succulent variety adapted to cooler mountain microclimates in Benguet and highland plateaus, producing heavy, dense 300–400 g bunches with superior crispness.
